newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Policeman killed in tense Albanian town of Vlore.
newsitem.headline: Policeman killed in tense Albanian town of Vlore.

text.p: An Albanian policeman was shot dead on Wednesday in the southern port town of Vlore, where three people died early this week in anti-government protests.
An Interior Ministry statement said the policeman was shot dead by automatic gunfire near his home in the Adriatic town, scene of clashes between riot police and protesters on Monday and Tuesday.
It identified the policeman as Shezai Zani, 30. Reporters in Vlore said a car had sped through the town during the day with someone firing an automatic rifle from the window.
Vlore police chief Ethem Kurti told Reuters Zani was shot while drinking coffee at a cafe near his home in the suburbs. He died immediately.
Kurti said Zani was in charge of guarding "places of special importance" and had not taken part in the clashes earlier this week.
"We don't know the motive for his killing," he said.
An anti-government protester was shot dead and two others died of heart attacks during clashes in Vlore this week. About 150 people were injured in the clashes.
Albania has been rocked by anti-government protests and clashes during the past month after several get-rich-quick investment schemes collapsed.
Irate investors in Europe's poorest state, which emerged from 40 years of isolation and Stalinism in 1990, blamed the right-wing government of President Sali Berisha.

The protesters blame the Berisha government for permitting the dubious schemes to flourish. Opposition parties have said his Democratic Party used money from the schemes to finance a winning election campaign last year.
